_comment: Hand-built citation ground truth for the 'Citation Graph Benchmark' collection in the Zotero test profile. Every edge below was read out of the citing PDF's own reference list and verified by four independent probes (DOI string, full title, bibliographic signature, author+year proximity); false positives were rejected by hand. This file is the reference answer that edge strategies are scored against - it is NOT derived from any strategy's output, and in particular not from OpenAlex.
_whatCountsAsAnEdge: An edge is a citation from one work in this 14-work collection to ANOTHER WORK IN IT. It is not a reference. These papers cite 1512 works between them; only 30 of those references point at a work the collection also holds, and those 30 are the edges. Everything else a paper cites is a ghost node outside the collection and the key says nothing about it. So barry2020 has 454 references and 6 edges, and sturner2019 has 35 references and 5 edges - those are complete counts, not samples.
_completenessCheck: The edge list was checked for completeness against Crossref's deposited reference lists on 2026-09-11, independently of the hand reading and of OpenAlex (which had already been scored here). For all 12 source works that have a DOI, the set of in-collection targets Crossref reports matches this file exactly, work for work: sarkar2023 6, sturner2019 5, zhang2022 4, barry2020 6, rondin2014 3, barry2016 1, dolde2011 1, hahn1950 0, dreau2011 2, gruber1997 0, magnard2020 0, blais2021 1 = 29, plus odmrManual's 1 (no DOI, hand-read from its PDF) = 30. No edge is missing and none is invented. refCount values are Crossref's exact figures, replacing the bracket-number estimates the first version carried. magnard2020's 0 is the point of that work: Crossref's deposit for it lists 52 DOIs and 10.1103/RevModPhys.93.025005 is not among them, so the title-match trap in expectedNonEdges is a non-edge on the machine evidence as well as the hand reading.

expectedNonEdges.why: The string 'spin echoes' DOES occur in dolde2011's reference list - inside the title of a DIFFERENT reference: 'van Oort, E. et al. Electric field induced modulation of spin echoes of NV centers in diamond, Chem. Phys. Lett. 168, 6 (1990)'. Substring matching on the two-word title 'Spin Echoes' emits a false edge here.
'Zhang' appears in barry2020 as 'Bluvstein, Zhang and Jayich 2019' - a different Zhang. Also chronologically impossible: 2020 cannot cite 2022.
'Zhang' appears in rondin2014 as 'Babinec ... Y. Zhang, J. R. Maze ...' - a different Zhang. Also chronologically impossible.
zhang2022 cites an IEEE Trans. Instrum. Meas. paper (Zhang 2020, TIM 69, 4370, doi 10.1109/TIM.2019.2949321) - same journal as sarkar2023, different paper. Also chronologically impossible.
A reader would expect this review to cite Gruber 1997, but it does not: the string 'gruber' occurs zero times in the whole PDF. Verified, not assumed.

THE REVERSE OF A REAL EDGE, which is why this pair is in the set. blais2021 -> magnard2020 is genuine, so a strategy that also draws this one puts a two-work CYCLE in the graph, and a cycle between two works is the visible symptom rather than the defect. magnard2020 does not cite the Blais review: Crossref's 54 deposited references do not list 10.1103/RevModPhys.93.025005, the PDF's 65 /URI annotations do not point at it, and 'Grimsmo' occurs zero times in the file. What the reference list DOES contain is the phrase 'circuit quantum electrodynamics' twice, both times inside the title of a DIFFERENT reference: '... Microwave-induced amplitude and phase-tunable qubit-resonator coupling in circuit quantum electrodynamics, Phys. Rev. A 91, 043846 (2015)' and 'Microwave-Controlled Generation of Shaped Single Photons in Circuit Quantum Electrodynamics, Phys. Rev. X 4, 041010 (2014)'. Substring matching on the title 'Circuit quantum electrodynamics' emits a false edge from each. Two guards that catch the other traps both fail here: minTitleLength does not, because the normalised title is 31 characters against a floor of 30; and rejectImpossibleYear does not, because it allows one year of slack for preprint/issue-date mismatches and 2021 is exactly one year past 2020.
'Zhang' appears in magnard2020 as 'Y. P. Zhang' (ref [31]) and 'Y. Zhang' (ref [34]) - different Zhangs. Also chronologically impossible.
Same surname collision in a 527-reference list, and 2021 cannot cite 2022.
adam2017 shares no domain with the rest of the set. Zero edges out.
No work in the set cites Adam. Zero edges in.

summary.edgesPdfReachableNote: 28 of the 30 edges have a citing work whose PDF the collection holds; those are the only ones a PDF-reading strategy can possibly find. The other 2 are from dreau2011, which is held without a PDF, and were confirmed against Crossref's deposited reference lists after edges/openalex.js proposed them. Score offline strategies against the 28 and anything with a metadata source against all 30 - the scorer reports both.
summary.edgesItemLevelNote: 28 edges between WORKS. dolde2011 is held as two items, so a scorer that works at item level and expands the duplicate on both sides sees 34. Score at work level; the 6-edge gap is the duplicate-merging penalty.
summary.channelsNote: A citation reaches a strategy through one of three INDEPENDENT channels, and each edge is flagged for all three. 'doi'/'title' are about the PRINTED text as PDF extraction yields it. 'pdfLink' is the link layer: a /URI annotation on the reference, which a reader never sees and which survives even when the printed entry carries neither a title nor an identifier. The pdfLink flags were extracted from raw PDF bytes by an independent parser (inflating object streams and reading /URI dicts), NOT from edges/pdfLinks.js output.
summary.ceilingTitleMatchExact: 19 of 28 (68%) - 20 edges carry a title, but dolde2011->gruber1997 does not survive exact normalised matching (mangled spacing). sturner2019->rondin2014 is already counted as title:false (truncated).
summary.theOneUnreachableEdge: dolde2011 -> gruber1997. Its printed title is mangled by extraction ('scanningconfocal optical microscopyand...'), the citing PDF carries no DOI in that entry, and Dolde 2011 has ZERO link annotations. Nothing but fuzzy title matching or author-year parsing can reach it.
summary.correctionNote: An earlier version of this file claimed a 78% ceiling on the grounds that the 6 barry2020 edges were 'unreachable without author-year parsing'. That was wrong: it only considered the printed text. The Reviews of Modern Physics PDF carries 435 /URI annotations, so all 6 of those references are DOI-linked in the link layer even though the printed entry is bare author-year. edges/pdfLinks.js finds all 6.
